title: Common Ground's separation of data from applications is the Powerhouse architecture in the customer's own vocabulary
content:
The mechanism is a Common Ground component dispatching typed operations on case decisions. The more useful observation is rhetorical: "separate data from applications" is a Common Ground slogan and also a description of what a Powerhouse record layer does. The architectural argument does not have to be introduced to this audience, only instantiated.

That changes the shape of the conversation. With most cohorts the first job is establishing that the record belongs outside the application; with these suppliers that premise is already institutional, and the discussion starts at whether Powerhouse is a credible component within their reference architecture.

All five leads are Dutch and arrived through the Benelux-suppliers research pass, with source rows naming Open Zaak, KISS, FSC, Nextcloud and GZAC proof-of-concept participation alongside Common Ground itself. Priorities are spread across "1 · parallel track", "1 · start here", "2 · next" and two at "3 · later". Public-sector case handling with an existing componentisation mandate is the closest thing in the corpus to a pre-qualified architectural fit.
